# Llama Stack GA-readiness assessment and definitive GA scope

## Description

Resolve the strategy's central unknown: the full inventory of gaps between the
current Tech Preview quality of Llama Stack and the GA bar. TP feedback is
scattered across support tickets and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has
been done. This epic consolidates that feedback, assesses each GA-bar dimension
the strategy names — API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling —
and produces the definitive GA scope that the stability, hardening, and
support-posture work is sized and re-baselined against. This is analytical work:
it inventories and decides scope; it does not implement fixes.

## Scope

- Compile TP feedback scattered across support tickets into a single structured
  gap inventory.
- Assess current Llama Stack distribution quality against the GA bar for each of
  the four named dimensions: API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error
  handling.
- Classify each identified gap by severity and GA-bar relevance (GA blocker,
  should-fix, accepted-with-documented-limitation).
- Produce the definitive GA scope document: what the GA release must fix, what it
  documents as a limit, and what is explicitly deferred.
- Distinguish gaps that require new evidence (for example scale-limit
  measurements) from gaps that will be addressed by declaring limits in the
  supported configuration matrix rather than producing that evidence.
- Ratify the resulting scope with product and support stakeholders.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the scattered TP feedback sources, when the assessment completes, then a
  single consolidated gap inventory exists covering API stability, upgrade
  paths, scale limits, and error handling.
- Every inventory entry names the gap, its GA-bar relevance, and a severity
  classification.
- The definitive GA scope document is produced and ratified by stakeholders, and
  is sufficient to size the downstream stability, hardening, and support-posture
  work without further discovery.
- Gaps requiring newly produced evidence are explicitly distinguished from gaps
  handled by declaring limits as unsupported.
- Measured by: downstream GA work can be planned from the assessment output
  without re-running discovery.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP
  quality and GA bar, producing the definitive GA scope.

## Open Questions from Strategy

- The strategy's open question — the GA scope depends on this assessment and the
  size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate until it lands — is
  the question this epic exists to answer.

# Llama Stack API stability guarantee and GA-bar hardening

## Description

Deliver the published API stability guarantee for Llama Stack at GA: versioned
APIs, a deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP
releases, plus closure of the GA-bar gaps confirmed by the GA-readiness
assessment within the definitive GA scope. This epic is the core engineering
hardening work of the graduation; its precise scope is re-baselined against the
assessment's gap inventory before implementation proceeds.

## Scope

- Version the published Llama Stack API surface (the OpenAI-compatible REST API
  surface and the provider-plugin configuration surface of the distribution).
- Define and publish the API deprecation policy covering that surface.
- Implement and test the upgrade path from the last two TP releases to the GA
  release.
- Remediate the GA-bar gaps confirmed by the readiness assessment within the
  definitive GA scope, including error-handling and scale-limit hardening of the
  published surface where the assessment classifies them as in scope.
- Stay within GA-bar quality work: new Llama Stack feature development beyond
  that, and deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths, are out of scope per
  the strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the published Llama Stack API surface, when the GA release ships, then
  the surface is versioned and the versioning scheme is documented.
- A deprecation policy is published and applies to the GA API surface.
- Given a Llama Stack distribution deployed on either of the last two TP
  releases, when it is upgraded to the GA release, then the upgrade succeeds —
  measured by executed upgrade-test coverage from both TP versions.
- No gap classified as a GA blocker by the readiness assessment remains open at
  GA.
- No new feature development beyond GA-bar quality work is included in the
  release.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): published API surface carries a stability guarantee — versioned
  APIs, deprecation policy, tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases.
- Implements the remediation side of HLR-1's output: closes the assessed GA-bar
  gaps within the definitive GA scope.

## Gating

- Gated by the GA-readiness assessment (Investigation): if the assessed gap
  inventory differs materially from the current estimate, this epic's scope is
  rewritten against the definitive GA scope before implementation; it is not
  removed.

targets, a backport policy, and a supported configuration matrix. The

error-handling posture established by the GA-readiness assessment, so this epic

- Define and document SLO targets for the GA Llama Stack distribution.
- Define the backport policy: which release lines receive fixes and for how

- Publish the supported configuration matrix: supported provider and deployment
  configurations and their scale limits, per the assessment's findings.
- Explicitly mark configurations outside the matrix as unsupported.
- Ratify the posture with support and product stakeholders.

  documented as unsupported.

  recorded.
- Measured by: a user or support engineer can determine from the published

# TrustyAI guardrails as a supported Llama Stack distribution integration

## Description

Promote safety guardrails via TrustyAI from an experimental flag to a supported,
documented integration in GA Llama Stack distributions. Today the integration
exists only as an experimental opt-in; at GA it must be a supported
configuration of the distribution that enterprise customers can build on.

## Scope

- Remove the experimental flag so the TrustyAI guardrails integration is
  available as a supported configuration of the GA Llama Stack distribution.
- Validate that the integration functions as a supported configuration without
  the experimental flag, through the distribution's provider-plugin
  configuration surface.
- Document the integration from the distribution side as engineering reference
  documentation shipped with the distribution: how to configure TrustyAI
  guardrails in a GA distribution and what is supported. The user-facing
  documentation uplift incorporates this reference material by reference
  rather than re-authoring it.
- Preserve a per-distribution path to disable the guardrails integration
  (rollback and configurability).
- Integration-level tests cover the supported configuration.

End-to-end validation with the TrustyAI service and the TrustyAI team's support
commitment for the integration are tracked separately by the TrustyAI team.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the experimental flag is disabled, when TrustyAI guardrails are
  configured on a GA Llama Stack distribution, then the integration is
  available and functions as a supported configuration.
- Given the experimental flag is enabled, when TrustyAI guardrails are
  configured, then the integration functions identically as a supported
  configuration — the experimental flag no longer gates access to it, and
  legacy experimental opt-in configurations are not broken by the promotion.
- The integration is documented as a supported configuration of the GA
  distribution.
- Given the guardrails integration is disabled for a distribution, then the
  distribution continues to function without it (rollback path).
- Integration-level tests exercise the supported configuration and pass.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions — Llama Stack
  distribution side.

## Dependencies

- None: this work proceeds in parallel with the stability and hardening work on
  the published API surface; the guardrails integration builds on existing
  provider-plugin interfaces.

# Dashboard Llama Stack management enabled by default for entitled clusters

## Description

Enable Llama Stack management in the Dashboard by default for entitled
clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate. At GA, entitled customers see
Llama Stack management without any manual enablement step. The Dashboard is
already GA; this is a default-and-gating change on its existing per-component
feature-flag mechanism, not new management UI.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard enablement default so Llama Stack management is enabled
  by default for entitled clusters.
- Remove the Tech Preview opt-in gate so no manual configuration is required to
  see Llama Stack management on an entitled cluster.
- Preserve configurability of the enablement through the Dashboard's
  per-component feature-flag mechanism (OdhDashboardConfig) so administrators
  can disable or roll back the surfaces.
- Ensure existing opt-in configurations from the Tech Preview period continue
  to function without regression.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an entitled cluster, when the Dashboard loads, then Llama Stack
  management is enabled by default with no opt-in configuration required.
- Given a cluster without the necessary entitlement, then Llama Stack
  management surfaces are not enabled.
- Given the removal of the Tech Preview opt-in gate, then no manual opt-in step
  remains anywhere in the enablement flow.
- Given the Llama Stack Dashboard feature flag is disabled via configuration,
  then the Llama Stack management surfaces are not visible; given the feature
  flag is enabled — the new default for entitled clusters — then Llama Stack
  management is available with no opt-in step.
- Existing Tech Preview opt-in configurations continue to work after the
  default flip (no regression).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P1): the Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for
  entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate).

## Dependencies

- None: the Dashboard reads Kubernetes CRs and its own feature-flag
  configuration; the enablement default is a configuration change with no
  build-against artifact from the Llama Stack work, so it proceeds in parallel.
  Release-train coordination with the GA release is a scheduling concern, not a
  dependency.

architecture context files, so no onboarding chains are required. The central
structural fact of the strategy is its own open question: the definitive GA scope
